knowledge:
- key_parameters: maxseg=The maximum number of segments to fit ;; maxk=The maximum length of an individual segment, used to reduce computational complexity from quadratic to linear ;; what=Type of plot in plotAlongChrom, either "dots" or "heatmap" ;; sepPlot=Logical indicating whether to plot different hybridization channels/conditions separately ;; makeRasterImage=Logical indicating whether to use grid.raster (faster, default) or grid.rect for heatmaps ;; colHeatmap=Color palette/gradient function for the heatmap (e.g., colorRamp) ;; penalty=Penalty type in logLik, either "AIC" or "BIC" for model selection
- alternatives: Picard et al. segmentation software, which has O(N^2) memory complexity; tilingArray's segment function reduces this to O(N * maxk) by restricting maximum segment length
- when_to_use: Appropriate for identifying transcript boundaries in tiling microarray data or copy number variations (gains/losses) in arrayCGH data where probe effects have been normalized
- pitfalls: If the number of hybridization channels (hybes) is greater than 4, plotAlongChrom with what="dots" will force taking the average across all hybes unless heatmaps are used; the segmentation algorithm assumes that probe-specific hybridization effects have already been normalized away

workflows.name: piecewise_segmentation
workflows.intent: Fit a piecewise constant curve to sequential genomic data and select the optimal number of segments using AIC or BIC.
input: intensity_matrix.txt (matrix of normalized intensity values where rows represent genomic positions and columns represent replicates/samples)
workflows.stages: 1. Run segmentation using the segment function with specified maxk and maxseg constraints ;; 2. Plot penalized log-likelihoods using plotPenLL ;; 3. Identify the optimal number of segments using logLik with AIC or BIC penalties
workflows.code:
seg  = segment(gd$x, maxk=maxk, maxseg=maxseg)
s = segment(gd$x, maxk=lenx, maxseg=as.integer(nrSeg * 2.5))
plotPenLL(s)
which.max(logLik(s, penalty="AIC"))
which.max(logLik(s, penalty="BIC"))

workflows.name: along_chromosome_visualization
workflows.intent: Visualize genomic expression profiles and segmentation boundaries along a chromosome region using dot plots or heatmaps aligned with GFF annotations.
input: segmentation_env.RData (R environment containing segmentation class objects named by chromosome and strand)
gff_annotation.gff (GFF table containing genomic features for the region of interest)
workflows.stages: 1. Plot expression data along the chromosome as a dot plot using plotAlongChrom ;; 2. Plot separate dot plots for different conditions using the sepPlot parameter ;; 3. Plot expression data as a heatmap using plotAlongChrom with what="heatmap" ;; 4. Optimize heatmap rendering speed and color palettes using makeRasterImage and colHeatmap
workflows.code:
plotAlongChrom(segnf,chr=1, coord=c(35000,50000),what="dots", gff=gffSub)
plotAlongChrom(segObj,chr=1, coord=c(35000,50000),what="dots", gff=gffSub,sepPlot = T)
plotAlongChrom(segnf,chr=1, coord=c(35000,50000),what="heatmap", gff=gffSub,
         rowNamesHeatmap=nmLabel,makeRasterImage=FALSE)
plotAlongChrom(segnf,chr=1, coord=c(35000,50000),what="heatmap", gff=gffSub,
         rowNamesHeatmap=nmLabel,makeRasterImage=TRUE)
plotAlongChrom(segnf,chr=1, coord=c(35000,50000),what="heatmap", gff=gffSub,
         rowNamesHeatmap=nmLabel,makeRasterImage=TRUE,
         colHeatmap = colorRamp(brewer.pal(9, "Blues")))
